entities.summary: Franklin Stewart Harris was president of Brigham Young University (BYU) from 1921 to 1945, and president of Utah State Agricultural College (USAG) from 1945 to 1950. His administration was the longest in BYU history and saw the granting of the first master's degrees. Under his administration the school became an accredited university. He set up several colleges, such as the College of Fine and Performing Arts, with Gerrit De Jong as the founding dean. Harris was an agricultural scientist, holding a doctorate in agronomy from Cornell University.
